description:
Analyze the spatial distribution of cells in a fluorescence microscopy image using Fiji's Distance Transform tools.

1. Open the image at `~/Fiji_Data/workspace/cell_image.tif` (scale: 1 px = 0.65 µm).
2. Segment the cells (Background Subtraction -> Threshold -> Watershed).
3. Use 'Analyze Particles' to extract cell centroids and areas.
4. Generate a Euclidean Distance Map (EDM) of the *intercellular space* (invert mask -> Process > Binary > Distance Map).
5. Save the EDM image to `~/Fiji_Data/results/spacing/distance_map.tif`.
6. Measure EDM statistics (mean, max) to quantify gap sizes.
7. Calculate Nearest-Neighbor (NN) distances for all cells.
8. Save per-cell data to `~/Fiji_Data/results/spacing/cell_measurements.csv` (columns: cell_id, centroid_x, centroid_y, area_px, nn_dist).
9. Save a summary report to `~/Fiji_Data/results/spacing/spacing_report.txt` with keys: num_cells, cell_coverage_percent, mean_nn_distance_px, edm_mean_px, edm_max_px.
10. Save a visual QC overlay (original image + cell outlines) to `~/Fiji_Data/results/spacing/qc_overlay.png`.
